key_insight: A MicroUS-specific foundation model pretrained on over 1.7 million unlabeled prostate ultrasound images enabled more data-efficient segmentation and lesion localization than generic pretrained or randomly initialized models.
clinical_relevance: This could help reduce expert annotation needs and accelerate development of automated tools for prostate MicroUS biopsy guidance and image interpretation.
method: Pretrained {micro}FM with DINOv2-style self-supervised learning on 1,736,391 unlabeled images from 780 patients.
Fine-tuned the model on three tasks: prostate capsule segmentation, urethra segmentation, and prostate cancer lesion localization.
Compared performance under limited annotation against random initialization and foundation models pretrained on natural, medical, and ultrasound images.
evidence_signal: In the 10% annotation setting, {micro}FM reached Dice scores of 93.8% for capsule segmentation and 58.4% for urethra segmentation, with lesion localization around 0.75 sensitivity at two false positives per 3D volume.
watch_item: The model was pretrained retrospectively at a single institution and did not include explicit 3D modeling, which may limit generalizability.
paper_title: Data-Efficient Prostate Micro-Ultrasound Image Analysis using a Modality-specific Foundation Model
